chapter: Fletcher as a leader and early bandmates
title: Benny Carter embarrasses a cocky Michigan pianist by changing keys
summary: At a late-night jam, a local pianist with pet keys challenged Benny Carter, who answered by playing through C sharp, A natural, F sharp and E natural until the pianist could not follow.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Oh. Why don't we go ahead. He's just a couple down the list, so we might as well.

Well, this happened in Michigan too. It seems like everything is Michigan. This was a jam session after the job. I'll never forget, Benny had his alto. He wasn't playing something then. And he very seldom jammed, but on this particular night he didn't feel like going to bed. He wanted to go out, and the guys told him, well, there's a club band that's open late, you know, and the guys jam down there, so we'll go.

I can't recall the club. It's not important, I guess, but nevertheless they had a little piano player there. I remember his name was Guy Rodgers. He was a local little boy. And he had a few pet keys he could play in, and, of course, he did not know Benny Carter. He didn't know him musically. He might have known his name, but he didn't know that Benny was a genius. So he wanted to play one of those standard

tunes. I don't know, but it was something like "Sweet Sue," It's been so long now, It's been so long now, but all I can remember is the incident. But they started out playing in G, you know, and they went to F and one of those things. He told Benny, say, "We're going to change keys now, says, let's go to C sharp." Benny says, "Well, I don't know. I'll try." Putting him on, you know.

But the more -- and, you know, And the little guy thought he was so and so. So Benny played one in D flat and struggled through it, but, you know, purposely. And then the little guy says, "Well, I'm going to A natural now. You know, if you get lost, --"

I'm sitting there, man. -- "If you get lost, you know, just lay out, and I'll pick you up, one of those things, see. So when they got there, he didn't have to -- this little piano player played. Benny started to come down. He played A natural. But when he finished the, by the time he got to his 30th bar over a 32 bar chorus course, Benny said, "let's go to F sharp." Benny got in F sharp and started to -- the guy looked about and one of those things. He played all through F sharp. Piano player couldn't even find the chords in F sharp. Benny says, "How about E natural, concert, one of those things. Won't you start playing. Why Benny was playing a solo by himself.
Then when they got through, this guy says, 'Who's this?' He says, 'That's Benny Carter, one of the greatest arrangers in the -- and the guy wanted to go through the floor.
That was one of the funniest things, man, and I sat there and just howled. And it was all in fun, you know. But we had a little fresh guy that knew a couple of pet tunes --
So I think that cured him.
So that -- these are funny things you never forget.
